newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins dip in thin trade ahead US holiday.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins dip in thin trade ahead US holiday.

text.p: Russian MinFin bond prices eased on Friday but few deals were struck as players were reluctant to open positions ahead of the long U.S. weekend, dealers said.
Monday is Martin Luther King Day in the U.S.
"It is a shorter working day in the West and Russian banks have done nothing notable either," one dealer said.
"Some deals were seen, but it is Friday, everything is calm ahead of a long U.S. weekend and there is no important news," said Sberbank dealer Sergei Abramov.
Russia's intention to treat non-residents equally on the government securities market by the end of 1997 would not have a direct impact on MinFins but could help improve sentiment.
"Russia would then seem a more open country for foreign investors," he said.

Central bank First Deputy Chairman Sergei Aleksashenko said on Friday that non-residents, who were only allowed to officially trade T-bills in Russia early last year, will be treated just like Russians by the end of 1997.
